grammar.rationale: Permissions may be direct or embedded as class-specific exceptions to prohibitions. Representative definitions are owner-relative and expand only an operative reference to representatives. Consent and purpose exceptions are preserved but do not become unrestricted class permissions. An outsider prohibition does not contradict sharing with representatives because representatives are outside its recipient scope. Relevant norms that leave a hypothesis open support NotMentioned; absence of any relevant root remains unhandled.

value.rationale: The grammar separates operative disclosure permissions and prohibitions from recitals and role definitions. It preserves recipient ownership, bounded exceptions, conditions, and the distinction between all third parties and persons outside a recipient-plus-representative group. The consumer proves the two fixed hypotheses only from relevant root norms; descriptions and definitions can interpret a norm but never create permission by themselves.
